data.title: Tokyo Inflation Accelerated, Keeping BOJ Rate Hike in Play
data.description:
By Megumi Fujikawa

TOKYO--Consumer inflation in Japan's capital picked up in November, reinforcing market expectations that the Bank of Japan will raise interest rates again next month.

Core consumer inflation in the Tokyo metropolitan area, which excludes volatile fresh food prices, climbed 2.9% in November from a year earlier, compared with October's 2.6% rise, government data showed Friday.

That was roughly in line with the 3.0% increase expected in a poll of economists by data provider Quick. The Tokyo figures are closely watched as a leading indicator of nationwide price trends.

The firmer reading strengthens the case for the BOJ to further tighten monetary policy at its final meeting of the year on Dec. 17-18. The central bank raised its policy rate to 1.25% in September and stated last month that underlying inflation had reached its 2% target.

The BOJ has said that consumer prices face upward pressure from higher crude oil costs amid Middle East tensions, a weak yen and rising prices for electronics components tied to artificial-intelligence demand.

BOJ Gov. Kazuo Ueda warned in Parliament last week that core consumer inflation is likely to climb well above 2%, reiterating the bank's readiness to raise interest rates further.

On Thursday, hawkish BOJ policy board member Naoki Tamura also urged the central bank to bring the policy rate toward a neutral level soon and act swiftly if upside price risks build. He said it is possible to assess financial conditions within a few months of each rate hike.

Write to Megumi Fujikawa at megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com

data.title: Korea pulls the plug on crypto barons' grip over exchanges
data.description:
IntelliNews summary:

  • Banks must jointly own more than half of an issuer, but a fintech can be the largest shareholder; issuers need KRW5bn ($3.7mn) of capital and full reserves.
  • Crypto exchange owners would be capped at 20%, or 34% with approval, hitting Upbit, Bithumb and GOPAX's controlling shareholders.
  • Korea's exchange market has shrunk to KRW58.9 trillion from KRW110.5 trillion at end-2024.
  • In Tokyo, SBI, SMFG and the Solana Foundation began full operations at SBI Solana Global on November 25.

____________________

South Korea's financial regulator wants banks to own most of any won-stablecoin issuer, under a draft digital asset law that would also end a nine-year ban on coin offerings.

Only consortiums in which banks together hold more than 50% would be licensed to issue 'digital payment tokens', the bill's legal term for stablecoins, in the first stage, the Financial Services Commission (FSC) said in a statement after a meeting of its Virtual Asset Committee on November 24. Any fintech or tech firm could still be the largest single shareholder and issuers would require FSC approval, to hold at least KRW5bn ($3.7mn) of equity capital and also have an approved issuance plan. They would also have to keep reserves of at least 100% of coins in circulation with an institution such as a bank, redeem at face value on demand and pay holders no interest.

The bank-majority rule settles, for now, the argument that has held up won stablecoins since President Lee Jae-myung promised them during his 2025 campaign. The Bank of Korea opposed private issuance on monetary-policy and financial-stability grounds, while the FSC and many lawmakers resisted rules that would shut fintech firms out. The FSC has split the difference: banks own the issuer, technology firms can run it. Lenders have been positioning for exactly that outcome, with Hana Financial Group buying 6.55% of Upbit operator Dunamu this year, after regulators said in January they would unwind a 2017 policy that kept financial firms out of crypto businesses.

Coins with more than KRW1 trillion in circulation could be designated systemic, bringing tougher capital and liquidity rules and the right for the Bank of Korea to demand a joint examination of the issuer. Foreign issuers could operate if supervised at home, with a local office and FSC registration; unapproved coins could not be listed or traded.

Smaller players read the stablecoin rules as a closed door. 'For smaller companies, this could effectively be interpreted as being told not to do business in South Korea,' an official at a smaller crypto exchange told the Korea Herald.

Exchange owners face a sell-down

The bill would treat licensed exchanges as market infrastructure and cap any one shareholder at 20%, or 34% with FSC approval, stripping voting rights above the limit. Existing operators would get three years to comply after designation, with up to three more for smaller exchanges.

Largest shareholder's stake in each Korean crypto exchange against the draft bill's limits. Source: FSC draft digital asset bill, November 24, 2026; stakes as reported by The Korea Times, November 25. IntelliNews

Every major exchange owner is above that line. Dunamu chairman Song Chi-hyung at present holds 25.51% of the Upbit operator which itself is in the midst of a share swap that would fold it into Naver Financial; Bithumb Holdings owns 73.56% of Bithumb; and Binance holds 67.45% of GOPAX, according to the Korea Times. The draft carries no forced-sale clause, but an FSC official said at a briefing that corrective orders could be issued and that companies 'would need to rectify the violation before pursuing other businesses or obtaining additional regulatory approvals'. The National Assembly Research Service warned in March that forcing shareholders to sell lawfully acquired stakes could be unconstitutional.

Coin offerings would return under a prospectus-style regime, with a white paper filed with the FSC, a cooling-off period and strict liability for false or missing information.

Domestic exchanges held KRW58.9 trillion of crypto assets at the end of June, down from KRW110.5 trillion at end-2024, and average daily trading fell to KRW3.1 trillion in 1H26, 44% less than in the previous half, according to the half-yearly survey by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit and the Financial Supervisory Service. Seoul has also proposed delaying its crypto gains tax to 2029, pending parliament's approval.

Market capitalisation on domestic crypto exchanges at end of period and average daily trading volume, KRW trillion, 1H24-1H26. Source: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit and Financial Supervisory Service half-yearly VASP surveys. IntelliNews

Tokyo's megabank goes live

A day after the FSC meeting, SBI Holdings, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG) and the Solana Foundation announced in a joint release that SBI R3 Japan had begun full-scale operations as SBI Solana Global, a joint venture of the three. It will build stablecoin payment rails, including micropayments by AI agents, tokenise bonds, funds and loan receivables, digitise real-world assets and run on-chain asset management, starting in Japan before moving across Asia.

The venture formalises a collaboration announced in July, when SBI listed support for stablecoins including JPYSC among its first tasks. None of the partners has disclosed stake sizes, capital or launch dates for products. The Solana Foundation put the two Japanese groups' combined assets at more than $2.3 trillion and their customer base at over 80mn, The Block reported, adding that the foundation is also working with Shinhan Card, Toss Bank and two Korean asset managers on stablecoin payments and tokenisation.

Japan dealt with the question Seoul is still legislating in 2022, when it amended its Payment Services Act to let banks, trust companies and licensed money-transfer firms issue fiat-backed coins. That leaves one of its three megabanks free to back a venture built on a public blockchain without waiting on parliament. KB Financial Group has run a trial of won-coin payments and remittances to Vietnam, but Korean banks still need a law before they can issue.

Whether the 50%-plus rule shields the won or guarantees incumbents a slice of a new payments market depends on details left to presidential decrees, including the shareholder test for issuers after the first stage. The FSC wants a quick passage, but lawmakers already have more than a dozen competing bills before them, and nothing changes until the National Assembly votes.

data.title: Theta Gold Mines Targets 1Q27 First Gold Pour as TGME Nears Completion
data.description:
Theta Gold Mines is targeting its first gold pour in the March quarter of 2027 as construction of its Transvaal Gold Mining Estates (TGME) project in South Africa approaches completion.

Executive chair Bill Guy outlined progress at the annual general meeting in Sydney on 27 November, with construction of the gold processing plant 81% complete and development expenditure estimated at A$84.8 million (US$56m) to the end of October.

The company has completed two drawdowns under its Nordic bond financing and has stockpiled 110,000 tonnes of ore in preparation for plant commissioning.

Theta Gold holds a 74% interest in the project in Mpumalanga province, where its revised feasibility study completed in February outlined a 13.1-year operating life.

Bond Funding Support

The A$136.4m (US$90m) senior secured bond issue Theta completed in June provides funding for project development over a four-year term at an annual coupon rate of 12.75%, with interest payable quarterly in advance.

Theta completed the second drawdown on 25 November, taking total proceeds released under the facility to A$109.6m (US$72.6m), with further releases dependent on construction funding requirements and cost-to-complete tests.

The company reported an existing cash balance of approximately A$96.2m (US$63.52m) at 25 November, with an undrawn bond balance of A$20.8m (US$13.7m).

The remaining facility includes a provision for cost overruns subject to approval by independent technical engineer Behre Dolbear Australia, which monitors the project build.

Processing Plant Advancing

The first shipment of 17 containers of crushing and screening equipment has arrived on-site, with a second shipment of 14 containers expected by 18 December to support installation of the three-stage circuit.

Theta has contracted the supply of two ball mills, with the twin-mill configuration designed to improve operational flexibility and allow maintenance without relying on a single mill.

The gold room is nearing completion, while gold casting equipment is already on-site and a furnace has been purchased for smelting and refining the metal ahead of the production start-up.

A new Siton underground drill rig has also arrived to support mechanised mine development ahead of production from underground workings.

The project schedule targets dry commissioning in the December quarter and completion of commissioning in the March quarter, with the timing of first gold subject to outstanding regulatory approvals.

Staged Underground Mining Plan

The development plan calls for initial production from existing rock dumps and tailings while Theta Gold undertakes an 18-month pre-development period at the Beta mine before extracting ore from its underground stopes.

Mining at Rietfontein is scheduled to start in the December quarter of 2028, followed by a planned increase in production from the Clewer-Dukes Hill-Morgenzon and Frankfort mines.

The February feasibility study forecasts recovery of 871,000 ounces of gold over the planned operating life at an average recovered grade of 4.28 grams per tonne, with peak annual production of approximately 115,000oz.

Theta has identified 43 historical gold mines across its holdings, with only four included in the current mine plan and approximately 3,000,000oz of gold resources outside that plan.

data.title: Core inflation in Japan's capital accelerates in November
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nov core CPI rises 2.9% yr/yr vs forecast +3.0%
  • Index excluding fresh food, energy rises 2.5% yr/yr
  • BOJ next meets Dec 17-18, markets expect rate hike to 1.5%

By Leika Kihara and Takahiko Wada

Annual core inflation in Japan's capital accelerated in November and stayed above the central bank's 2% target for three straight months, highlighting mounting price pressure and bolstering the case for a near-term interest rate hike.

The data, widely regarded as a leading indicator of nationwide trends, will be among factors the Bank of Japan scrutinises in deciding whether to raise interest rates at its next two-day policy meeting ending on December 18.

The core consumer price index, which includes prices of fuel but not fresh food, in Tokyo rose 2.9% in November from a year earlier, data showed on Friday, compared with the median market forecast of 3.0%. It followed a 2.6% gain in October.

An index stripping away the effect of volatile fresh food and fuel prices, which is closely watched by the BOJ as a more accurate gauge of trend inflation, rose 2.5% in November after a 2.6% gain in October, the data showed.

data.title: Brent crude crosses $96 a barrel mark after Houthis attack key Saudi refinery
data.description:
Crude oil prices have edged higher during a thin volume holiday trading session on Friday, November 27, after an attack on a key refinery in Saudi Arabia.

Brent crude traded above the $96 a barrel mark for the January contracts, having already gained more than 6% in the previous two sessions. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) or the US crude futures for the January settlement are also trading 1.5% higher in early trading in Asia, close to the $85 a barrel mark.

Saudi Arabia's press agency reported citing an unnamed Energy Ministry source that the Iran-backed Houthis attacked the Jazan refinery on the Red Sea coast, halting some operations, killing one worker, and injuring many others.

The Jazan refinery has a capcity of 4,00,000 barrels per day and the attacks mark another blow to the oil infrastructure in the region that has been subject to multiple attacks in the recent days. Houthis on Wednesday also claimed to have attacked the key Ras Tanura refinery, which has a capacity of 5,00,000 barrels per day, a claim that the Saudi administration has not confirmed yet.

According to the UK Maritime Trade Operations, another tanker was struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, while Iran claimed, without independent confirmation, that several vessels hit mines in the key waterway.

Despite the attacks, shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has increased in November, as per data from Vortexa. These flows, coupled with the International Energy Agency (IEA) forecasting an oil surplus this quarter, have kept prices in check despite the recent attacks.

Trading volumes are expected to remain thin Thursday because of the US Thanksgiving holiday, which could exaggerate prices moves. West Texas Intermediate trades will be booked for Friday settlement.

(With Inputs From Agencies)

data.title: Powerful Storm Hits East Coast, Scrambling Thanksgiving Plans — WSJ
data.description:
By Victoria Albert

A major storm is scrambling Thanksgiving Day plans along the East Coast, with heavy winds and rain causing power outages, flight cancellations and the postponement of Macy's annual holiday parade.

The National Weather Service said widespread coastal flooding was under way along the mid-Atlantic and New England coastline, with "significant inundation" in Virginia, the Delaware Bay and parts of the Chesapeake Bay and southern New Jersey coast. Forecasters warned to expect flooded structures and impassable roads, as well as wind gusts of up to 60 mph along the coast and 50 mph further inland.

About 1 to 3 inches of rain are expected in the region, with the possibility of scattered flash flooding.

Footage from local news showed heavy flooding on some Virginia roads. Rich Otto, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service, said some parts of the state have already seen 2 to 4 inches of rain, though rainfall there is expected to ease as the storm crawls north.

As of early Thursday afternoon, more than 550,000 people were without power along the East Coast and mid-Atlantic, according to Poweroutage.us. The outages were concentrated in Maryland and Virginia, where energy-provider Dominion said broken utility poles and large trees on power lines meant it could be days before power was restored in some areas.

"Outages are especially difficult on a holiday, and we appreciate your patience as our crews work to get the lights back on," the utility said on social media.

Another 123,000 power outages were reported in Missouri, according to Poweroutage.us, after several inches of snow fell on the eastern side of the state. Some areas, including Ste. Genevieve, Mo., saw as much as 14 inches of snow, according to the National Weather Service.

Roughly 1,600 flights within, into or out of the U.S. have been delayed, and more than 400 have been canceled, according to flight-data specialist FlightAware. The hardest-hit airport thus far is Washington Dulles International Airport in Virginia.

In New York City, where fears of severe weather forced officials to postpone the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, wind gusts exceeding 30 mph were recorded across all five boroughs — including a 56 mph gust at LaGuardia Airport in Queens. The city's emergency-management department warned residents to secure loose outdoor items and use caution around trees and scaffolding.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani warned the city could see wind gusts as high as 65 mph. "If you're traveling, give yourself extra time," Mamdani warned Wednesday night. "And remember: No destination is worth risking your safety."

Write to Victoria Albert at victoria.albert@wsj.com
